milestones.description: mergeBacklogs drops the architect's added-requirement output whenever the architect's fresh IDs (numbered from P1, prompts.ts:134) collide with the patched backlog's IDs. Fix by renumbering colliding architect items against the patched ID space and APPENDING them, instead of skipping. See architecture/bug-001-backlog-merge.md.

tasks.description: Replace the three collision-skip branches (phase backlog-merger.ts:217, milestone :153, task :113) with renumber-and-append, using parent-context-aware renumbering so descendant IDs stay hierarchy-consistent. mergeBacklogs must remain a pure, synchronous transform and mergeBacklogs(empty, x) ≡ x.

subtasks.title: Add pure ID-renumbering helpers to backlog-merger.ts
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bug-001-backlog-merge.md §'Chosen fix'. The architect numbers IDs fresh from P1 (src/agents/prompts.ts:134) with no view of existing IDs, so collisions are the normal production case. Renumbering MUST be parent-context-aware (a pre-pass that renumbers all phases to maxPhase+1 is WRONG: folded-in milestones under a title-matched phase would get a mismatched prefix like P5.M1 under phase P1).
2. INPUT: The existing `collectIds(backlog): Set<string>` and `registerPhaseIds(phase, ids)` helpers already exist in src/core/backlog-merger.ts. The id regexes are in src/core/models.ts (Phase ^P\d+$, Milestone ^P\d+\.M\d+$, Task ^P\d+\.M\d+\.T\d+$, Subtask adds \.S\d+$).
3. LOGIC: Add pure helpers (no I/O, no logger side-effects) to src/core/backlog-merger.ts:
   - `maxPhaseNumber(reserved: Set<string>): number` — scan ids matching ^P(\d+)(\.M|$) → max+1.
   - `maxChildNumber(parentId: string, reserved: Set<string>, level: 'milestone'|'task'|'subtask'): number` — e.g. parentId 'P1', level 'task' → scan ^P1\.M(\d+)\.T(\d+) , return next task num for that parent's milestone chain. (For milestone level scan ^P1\.M(\d+); for subtask scan ^<taskId>\.S(\d+).)
   - `renumberPhase(phase, phaseNum, reserved): Phase` — deep clone with id `P{phaseNum}` and ALL descendants remapped to P{phaseNum}.M{k}.T{j}.S{l} sequentially; register every resulting id into `reserved`.
   - `renumberMilestone(ms, parentPhaseId, msNum, reserved): Milestone` — id `parentPhaseId.M{msNum}`, descendants consistent; register ids.
   - `renumberTask(task, parentMilestoneId, taskNum, reserved): Task` — id `parentMilestoneId.T{taskNum}`, subtasks remapped; register ids.
   Preserve every non-id field (title, status, description, story_points, dependencies, context_scope, prd_selectors) verbatim. Dependencies that reference remapped sibling ids must be rewritten to the new ids (map old→new within the renumbered subtree).
4. OUTPUT: Exported pure functions importable by the merge logic in S2. Each helper unit-tested: produces collision-free hierarchy-consistent ids; preserves non-id fields; `mergeBacklogs({backlog:[]}, x)` identity is unaffected (these helpers are additive).
5. MOCKING: None — pure data transforms; use plain Backlog literals in tests.
6. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change (internal helpers). Update the module's internal JSDoc only if a function's contract warrants it.

subtasks.title: Wire renumbering into mergeBacklogs/mergePhase/mergePhase (replace skip→renumber-append)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bug-001-backlog-merge.md. The three skip branches are: phase skip at backlog-merger.ts:217 (mergeBacklogs), milestone skip at :153 (mergePhase), task de-dup `continue` at :113 (mergeMilestone). The architect decomposes ONLY added requirements (decomposePRD feeds delta_prd.md only — prp-pipeline.ts:1295), so EVERY architect task is genuinely new; the task de-dup drop is therefore always wrong and must become renumber-and-append. Title-matching for extend (phase/milestone) is CORRECT and stays.
2. INPUT: The renumber helpers from P1.M1.T1.S1 (renumberPhase/renumberMilestone/renumberTask, maxPhaseNumber, maxChildNumber). `existingIds` Set and `phaseByTitle`/`msByTitle` maps already built in mergeBacklogs/mergePhase.
3. LOGIC: In src/core/backlog-merger.ts:
   - mergeBacklogs phase loop: when title NOT matched, if `!existingIds.has(archPhase.id)` append as-is (register ids) ELSE `renumberPhase(archPhase, maxPhaseNumber(existingIds), existingIds)` then register+append. Remove the warn-only skip `else` (keep a final defensive warn only if an id is STILL duplicated after renumber — should be unreachable).
   - mergePhase milestone loop: when title NOT matched, if no collision append as-is ELSE `renumberMilestone(archMs, existing.id, maxChildNumber(existing.id, existingIds, 'milestone'), existingIds)` then append.
   - mergeMilestone task loop: REPLACE the `if (existingIds.has) continue` drop. If no collision append as-is; if collision `renumberTask(archTask, existing.id, maxChildNumber(existing.id, existingIds, 'task'), existingIds)` then append. (Architect tasks are always new added-requirement tasks.)
   Invariant after change: NO architect item is ever dropped — every item either extends (title match, existing id kept) or appends (unique hierarchy-consistent id). mergeBacklogs stays pure + synchronous.
4. OUTPUT: mergeBacklogs(patched, architect) where architect items with colliding ids are REMAPPED and present in the result (not skipped). Consumed unchanged by prp-pipeline.ts:1046 and :1345.
5. MOCKING: logger() can be a no-op spy in tests; verify warn calls where relevant.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Correct the module header JSDoc 'Defensive ID-collision skips' paragraph in backlog-merger.ts to describe renumber-and-append (the skip is gone). No external doc change.
7. CORRECT EXISTING TESTS: tests/unit/core/backlog-merger.test.ts currently ASSERTS the drop as correct ('skips an architect phase whose id collides (despite a new title) and warns', the milestone variant, and 'de-duplicates a task whose id already exists (keeps patched status, warns)'). Rewrite these THREE to assert renumber-and-append: the new added item SURVIVES with a remapped unique id, the patched item is intact, and no data is lost. (TDD: write the new assertions first, watch them fail, implement, pass.)

subtasks.title: Wire classifyArtifactWithRetry guard into decomposePRD
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bug-002-classifiers.md §'Part B'. decomposePRD loads `prdContent = await loadDeltaPRD(sessionPath)` at prp-pipeline.ts:1295 (inside the `if (isDelta)` branch) and feeds it straight to the architect. classifyArtifactWithRetry(content: string): Promise<'CLEAN'|'DIRTY'> is in src/core/change-classifier.ts:257, protective default DIRTY. The action-on-DIRTY is the ONE ambiguous point: the bug report requires 'protection' but does not quote §4.3's exact wording.
2. INPUT: classifyArtifactWithRetry export from src/core/change-classifier.ts (add import). prdContent from loadDeltaPRD.
3. LOGIC: In src/workflows/prp-pipeline.ts decomposePRD, immediately AFTER `prdContent = await loadDeltaPRD(sessionPath)` (and BEFORE building the architect prompt), classify:
   const artifactVerdict = await classifyArtifactWithRetry(prdContent);
   if (artifactVerdict === 'DIRTY') { /* protective action per PRD §4.3 */ }
   ACTION-ON-DIRTY DECISION (MUST verify against PRD §4.3 before finalizing): the fail-safe default is to NOT feed malformed content to the architect unprotected — log a prominent warn and THROW (abort the breakdown) so the next run regenerates delta_prd.md via the delta spawn path. If §4.3 instead specifies warn-and-proceed, implement that. Because the protective default on classifier exhaustion is DIRTY, abort-on-DIRTY means classifier-down → breakdown aborts → next run retries (delta spawn regenerates delta_prd.md, so it re-classifies fresh input — no infinite loop). Record the chosen action + rationale in a code comment AND the commit message.
4. OUTPUT: delta_prd.md is classified before architect consumption; DIRTY content is never fed unprotected; CLEAN proceeds.
5. MOCKING: Unit-test by mocking classifyArtifactWithRetry → CLEAN (assert architect prompt built + agent called) and → DIRTY (assert architect NOT called, error thrown/warn logged). Mock loadDeltaPRD to return sample content.
